## Publish gate report

**Going out:** a creator post about a gifted product, UK audience, with no date given.

**Checks**
- **Claims:** no stats, rankings, guarantees or testimonials. "Lovely with oat milk" is a personal opinion about flavour, which the policy allows. Pass.
- **Regulated claims:** nothing on health, money, environment, children or prices. Pass.
- **House style:** short, plain and natural, with no AI tells. Pass.
- **Disclosure: fails.**
  - The post opens with "Pebblebrook sent me their winter sampler", which is the only hint of a gift, and it isn't a clear label. Free product is a material connection, so the post needs an upfront label such as "Gifted" before anyone engages with it. UK rules (ASA/CAP and CMA) expect this.
  - "Not paid to say that, just liked it" is misleading. It suggests there is no commercial relationship when the creator received free product. Even if no money changed hands, this line plays down the gift, so it should go.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite)**
> Gifted: Pebblebrook sent me their winter sampler. The rooibos chai is lovely with oat milk. Honest opinion, I liked it.

If the platform has a branded-content or paid-partnership tool, switch it on as well. Put the label on every post in a series.

**Needs a decision**
- Confirm that gifting is the whole relationship, with no fee, commission, affiliate link or editorial approval from Pebblebrook. If any of those apply, the label should be "Ad" or "Paid partnership" instead.
- Confirm that the creator agrees to the revised wording.

**Approver:** the policy names no approver, so the user (the account holder) needs to give an explicit yes to the revised text. Nothing should be published until they do, and I haven't recorded any approval.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "Pebblebrook sent me their winter sampler.", "type": "missing_disclosure"}, {"quote": "Not paid to say that, just liked it.", "type": "other"}], "publish": false}
```
